Fixed-point addition, sign change and power-of-two scaling as linear streaming operations.

differences.what: A's root claim draws the conclusion that n log n is not the optimal order of multitape multiplication. B never states the negation; neither gives the liminf formulation.

items.note: Only A connects the bound to the conjecture, and only by stating the conclusion.

chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route with intact dependencies. The networks with s<Wm come from labels L<N/2. The exact deficits fix tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. The recurrences give O(Ve^tau) interchange (via matrix shear) and O(Vd^{lambda'}) layers (via phase frames and packed additions). These feed transform layout, ring convolution, resampling, chirp and cancellation, exact recovery, and the cost table whose minimum margin epsilon c(1-tau)=2^{-181} sets kappa. A states the general recurrence up front (S1) and B after the networks (S2.7), and neither thins out anywhere the other does not.

errors.says: In general, a call at parameter mf costs s child calls on volume V/W plus O(V), so F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and F_k=O(m^{k tau}).
errors.paper: The O(1) per-volume overhead and the O(e^tau) solution hold for the interchange recurrence. For the numerical layer the node overhead is O((eK)^tau+1) and the result is O(d^{lambda'}). The introduction states only the factor s/W<m.

errors.says: A call at parameter mf (field digits or selected axes of a numerical layer, per S2.7a) gives F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and growth O(e^tau).
errors.paper: The numerical layer satisfies F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e) and total O(d^{lambda'}). The O(1) recurrence is the interchange's (line 1552).

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error, and the one minor overgeneralization of the recurrence is shared. The chains are equivalent. The deciding differences are in the derivations of core results. B alone states the label lemma's residual subspaces (L1, L2), the k-column factor count of the phase interface (P3), the identity D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and the DIF and reverse-procedure justification of B_t F_t^- and F_t^+ B_t^{-1}. A's advantages are fewer and mostly on supporting items: the alternating-plane absorption (L4), the dimension-exponent conditions, and the statement that n log n is not optimal.
